title: Replay of cached negative overlay verdict gives no indication it is cached
body:
Re-filed from `containers/storage#2402` (https://github.com/containers/storage/issues/2402), which was auto-closed by the migration bot with a pointer here. Content below is unchanged from the original.

---

## What happens

`drivers/overlay/overlay.go`: `cachedFeatureCheck` replays the recorded text of `<runhome>/overlay-true|false` verbatim on every driver init, with no indication at default log level that no live probe ran. Only `--log-level debug` mentions it (`Cached value indicated that overlay is not supported`).

Concrete case: a verdict recorded during a transient storage flap (`kernel does not support overlay fs: ... unlinkat .../overlay/compat496290003/merged/subdir/file: operation not permitted`) replayed byte-identically for days — including a `compat*` probe path that no longer existed on disk — while the store underneath was healthy (a live re-probe passes). That misdirection cost hours of kernel/filesystem debugging before anyone thought to `cat` the cache file. Deleting `<runhome>/overlay/overlay-false` (here `/run/user/1000/containers/overlay/overlay-false`) restored live probing immediately.

## Why the prior disposition is insufficient

containers/podman#12212 closed this failure class as "a configuration issue" on the grounds that runRoot belongs on tmpfs and the verdict therefore clears on reboot. That is load-bearing on reboot frequency: the documented contract is advisory (`containers-storage.conf(5)`: runRoot "should be on a tmpfs" — the same document reserves "must" for genuine requirements), while the cache design treats volatility as guaranteed (no TTL, no revalidation, no signal). Long-uptime machines (servers, lab fleets) go months without rebooting. The replay is indistinguishable from a live probe failure. And the probe can fail for transient environmental reasons (full disk, I/O error, bad ownership mid-migration) while the recorded message claims kernel non-support.

## Reproducer (validated)

```bash
# 1. Clear any cached positive verdict, then plant a stale negative:
rm -f /run/user/"$UID"/containers/overlay/overlay-true
echo 'kernel does not support overlay fs: planted stale verdict for repro' > /run/user/"$UID"/containers/overlay/overlay-false
# 2. Observe: fails with the planted text, no hint it is cached:
podman info 2>&1 | head -3
# 3. Contrast: only --log-level debug mentions caching:
podman --log-level debug info 2>&1 | grep -i 'cached value'
# 4. Clean up (deleting forces a live re-probe, which re-records the true verdict):
rm /run/user/"$UID"/containers/overlay/overlay-false
podman info --format '{{.Store.GraphDriverName}}'
```

Note: with a cached `overlay-true` present the plant is ignored (`cachedFeatureCheck` reads `*-true` first) — step 1's removal is load-bearing, not incidental. Steps 1-3 intentionally break podman use until step 4; `/run` being tmpfs, a reboot also clears everything.

## Checked permalinks (containers/storage, main branch)

- `drivers/overlay/overlay.go` L611 — `cachedFeatureCheck` (replay, debug-only logging)
- `drivers/overlay/overlay.go` L227 — `checkAndRecordOverlaySupport` (records the verdict)
- `drivers/overlay/overlay.go` L683 — `supportsOverlay` probe (`MkdirTemp(home, "compat")` + mount + `RemoveAll`, full cleanup in defer)
- `drivers/overlay/check.go` L228, L284 — sibling probes (`supportsIdmappedLowerLayers`, `supportsDataOnlyLayers`) use the same cache pattern (fine for graceful-degradation features)

## Ask

Minimal, no behavior change: when serving a cached negative verdict, log one warning-level line stating the verdict is cached and naming the file to remove to force a re-probe. Not asking to stop caching, add TTLs, or distinguish transient causes.
